sections.h2: Knox County tax offices and phone numbers
sections.html:
Five phone numbers cover nearly every Knox County tax question, and each office is in the Barbourville courthouse complex at 401 Court Square. The PVA sets the value. The sheriff bills and collects. The clerk takes over what goes unpaid, and the county attorney pursues it from there.

Who to call in Knox County
OfficeUse it forPhone
Property valuation administrator (PVA)Value, exemptions, appeal conferences(606) 546-4113
SheriffPaying the current bill(606) 546-3181
County clerkDeeds, delinquent certificates, filing an appeal(606) 546-3568
County attorneyDelinquent bills and payment talks(606) 546-9515
Fiscal courtGeneral county government(606) 546-6192

Courthouse doors open weekdays from 8:30 until 4:00. On Saturday mornings until noon, only the county clerk and circuit clerk offices stay open. To record a deed on a Knox County house, carry it to the clerk on the first floor.

Knox County had 30,193 residents in 2020 and an estimated 29,532 by July 2025. It holds 14,090 housing units, and about one in eight were empty at the 2020 count. A typical owner-occupied home is valued at $118,700, roughly two in three of the 11,711 households own, and a typical monthly rent is $681. At prices this low, a few thousand dollars of back tax takes a large bite out of a sale, so ask for payoff numbers before you list.

sections.h2: Which school district taxes your address
sections.html: Knox has three public school systems: Knox County Public Schools, Barbourville Independent and Corbin Independent. Two houses a few blocks apart can sit in different systems, and that shows up on the bill. Give the parcel number to the PVA or the sheriff and ask which district applies before you quote a price or compare bills.

Steady moisture and hard freezes put roofs, gutters, crawlspaces and exposed plumbing at the top of an inspector's list. If you keep receipts for recent repairs, or tell a cash buyer straight what needs work, the back-and-forth gets shorter. The same file supports an assessment conference if the PVA's value assumes a house in better shape than yours.

Kentucky bars an appeal until you have sat down with the PVA, so book that conference first. Once the May inspection window closes, the county clerk takes the appeal within a day, and a local board of fellow owners hears it a few weeks later.

Bring proof: photos, contractor bids, an appraisal or nearby sales. Show up with nothing and the board will deny you. The PVA appraises everything at full market price, so recent nearby sales make the strongest argument.

The year's property tax comes due at the end of December, and most Kentucky sheriffs begin collecting in October or November. Discount and penalty steps differ across counties, so read the dates printed on your Knox County bill or call the sheriff at (606) 546-3181.

Anything still owed on April 15 goes to the clerk as a certificate of delinquency with a lien on the parcel. The clerk offers a delinquent tax lookup, and the clerk's own figure controls at the time of sale. The state's worked example grows a $1,000 bill to $1,254 at transfer and to $1,659.90 after a June advertisement. Interest adds one percent per month.

  • The county attorney mails a 30-day letter, then a 60-day letter.
  • A sale to a third-party buyer can follow, 90 to 135 days after the transfer.
  • That buyer takes over the lien, and the owner then pays the buyer.

Whoever held title on January 1 personally owes the bill, and under KRS 134.420 the lien lasts eleven years whoever holds the deed. A buyer inherits it with the house, so sellers clear it first.

Anyone past their 65th birthday, and anyone ruled totally disabled by a retirement system, can deduct $49,100 from the assessed value for 2025 and 2026 if the house is their residence on January 1. File with the PVA by the end of December. Heirs living elsewhere do not inherit the break automatically.

sections.h2: Splitting taxes when a Knox County house sells
sections.html:
The bill carries the January 1 owner's name, so a March sale still leaves the seller as taxpayer of record. The closing agent splits the year on the settlement statement and pays the sheriff. KRS 382.135(1)(d) requires an in-care-of address on the deed for that year's bill, so supply the buyer's mailing address.

Heirs, owners behind on payments and landlords with a vacant rental often wonder whether a cash buyer can wrap up everything in one closing. It works when the payoffs are known first: the sheriff quotes the current-year amount and the clerk quotes any older certificate. Ask the county attorney's office as well whether a payment plan is on file, because the title agent will ask.

sections.h2: What to bring to the courthouse
sections.html:
Most of your errands happen under one roof, so one trip can cover several. For a conference with the PVA, bring the parcel number, your latest bill and whatever backs up your number: photos, contractor bids, an appraisal or recent nearby sales. For a homestead application, bring proof of age or a retirement system disability ruling, and file before the year ends.

At the clerk's office on the first floor, bring the signed deed if you are recording a sale, and ask for the delinquent certificate balance on the same visit. Keep each receipt. The title agent will want a record that the current year was paid or prorated, and a clean paper trail makes closing smoother for you and for the buyer.

sections.h2: Steps before you list a house with back taxes
sections.html:
Start with two phone calls. The sheriff gives you the current-year amount, and the clerk gives you the balance on any older certificate. Ask both for the figure in writing and for the date it stays good, since interest keeps running each month. If a payment plan exists, the county attorney's office at (606) 546-9515 can tell you where it stands.

Gather the deed, the most recent bill and any delinquent notice into one folder. Hand a copy to the title agent early. A cash sale skips the buyer's loan approval, so the only real delay is usually a payoff that nobody requested ahead of time. Once the figures are in hand, pick a closing date inside the window they cover. If the date slips, call both offices again for updated amounts, because interest and fees change the number from month to month.

faqs.q: Which office takes Knox County property tax payments?
faqs.a: The sheriff, at (606) 546-3181, collects the current bill. After April 15 the clerk, at (606) 546-3568, handles it as a delinquent certificate.

faqs.q: How do I begin disputing a Knox County property value?
faqs.a: Schedule a conference with the PVA at (606) 546-4113. Filing with the clerk comes afterward, before the deadline that follows the roll inspection.

faqs.q: How much does the Knox County homestead exemption remove?
faqs.a: It removes $49,100 of assessed value for 2025 and 2026 for qualifying seniors and totally disabled owners living in the house. Applications go to the PVA before the year ends.

faqs.q: Do late Knox County bills pick up interest?
faqs.a: Yes. After the bill reaches the clerk as a certificate, interest runs at one percent per month, with commissions and fees on top.

faqs.q: Could I sell a Knox County home that has unpaid tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The lien stays attached to the parcel, so the payoff is deducted at closing. Get written amounts from the sheriff and the clerk before you pick a date.
